issues.title: The run log records that both hooks passed their self-test
issues.body:
### Result
A run's event log says that both hooks passed their self-test, with the timing of each answer, so the evidence that the guardrails were in place is in the run's record and not only implied by the agent having started.

### Done when
- [ ] The tick logs one `hooks-checked` event before `picked`, with each hook's name, the three self-test outcomes (deny, allow, not-JSON) and the slowest answer in milliseconds
- [ ] A failed settings check or self-test logs the same event with the problems, before the tick exits with its existing code
- [ ] The event is in the public run artifact and in the evidence saved to the private repo, because it is part of the run's `.jsonl` log
- [ ] `docs/factory-trigger.md` names the event where it describes the self-test
- [ ] A test per bullet with a fake hook runner

### Must not break
- The exit codes of `factory:tick` for a failed settings check or self-test
- The 15-second hook time limit and the half-limit budget the self-test uses

### Why
Reading the first unattended run's log on 10 November, the only sign that the hooks were loaded and answering was that the agent started at all, plus two denials later in the transcript. A run with no denial would leave no positive evidence. The decision log's claim that every run starts behind working guardrails should be checkable from the run's own record.

### Out of scope
- Changing what the self-test checks

### Depends on

issues.title: Split factory-tick along its seams
issues.body:
### Result
`factory-tick.ts` is split along the seams it already has, and the side-effect layer that today is only exercised live gets tests through fixtures.

### Done when
- [ ] Modules: decisions (pure), ticket snapshot and provenance, workspace (lock, worktrees, teardown, fingerprints), agent (spawn, stream parsing), audit, verify, and the tick that wires them; `factory-tick.ts` keeps only the entry point
- [ ] The agent's stream-line parsing and the audit's result mapping are pure functions with fixture tests taken from real run logs
- [ ] No module is over 400 lines
- [ ] `factory-timeline.ts` uses the shared runs-directory function instead of its own copy
- [ ] Tests that pinned implementation (exact call arrays, exact problem counts, regex over the workflow file) are rewritten to pin behaviour, or kept with a comment saying what they protect

### Must not break
- `npm run factory:tick` on the PC and `--ci` in Actions
- Every stop path shown live on Day 4

### Why
The file is 1363 lines. Its pure part is well tested; the 500 lines of real side effects (lock, worktrees, audit API reads, verify, evidence saving) are tested only by running the factory. The seams are already visible in the file's structure.

### Out of scope
- Changing what the tick does

### Depends on
#108

issues.title: One GitHub helper and one paths module for every script
issues.body:
### Result
One `github.ts` module (the `gh` wrapper, paging, time limits, JSON parsing) and one `paths.ts` module (repo root, private directory, evidence directory, runs directory) used by every script. No script carries its own copy.

### Done when
- [ ] `packages/harness/src/github.ts` exports `gh`, `ghJson` and `ghAll` (paginate and flatten) with one time-limit policy; `review-wait`, `revert-check`, `rules-propose`, `ticket-ready` and `factory-tick` use it, and their own helpers are gone
- [ ] `packages/harness/src/paths.ts` resolves the repo root, the private directory (`FAULTFORGE_PRIVATE_DIR`, else the parent of `factory.json`'s evidence folder) and the evidence and runs directories in one place; `inject`, `rules-evidence`, `rules-propose`, `factory-tick` and `factory-timeline` use it
- [ ] A test shows that a non-default `evidence` path in `factory.json` is handled the same by every script
- [ ] Argument parsing uses `node:util` `parseArgs` in every script that takes options
- [ ] Line count of `packages/harness/src` goes down, and `npm run check` passes with no test changed except for the moved helpers

### Must not break
- Every command's options and exit codes
- The runner's stripped environment for `revert:check`

### Why
The scripts carry five copies of a `gh` helper with three different time-limit and buffer settings, compute the private directory four different ways, and parse arguments in five styles. Devil's Advocate and the report command will add more scripts; this is the moment to give them one foundation.

### Out of scope
- Moving logic into `packages/core` (#15); this ticket prepares it

### Depends on

issues.title: The runner runs revert:check itself before calling a PR ready
issues.body:
### Result
The runner's verify step runs `revert:check` itself on the PR the agent reports, instead of trusting the agent to have run it. A PR whose tests don't fail without its change (exit 1), or that can't be judged (exit 2), stops for the owner like any other failed verification.

### Done when
- [ ] `verifyPr` runs `npm run revert:check -- <repo> <pr>` after the review check, and exit 1 or 2 adds a problem naming the reason it printed
- [ ] The result is in the run log as a verify event, and its record is saved with the run's evidence
- [ ] The tests run in the runner with the stripped environment `revert:check` already uses: no factory secret reaches them
- [ ] A test covers each exit code's effect on the verification
- [ ] Shown live: one factory run whose PR is caught, and a drill whose tests pass without the change, stopped for the owner

### Must not break
- The other verify checks (open PR, the pushed commit, CI, the review) keep working and keep their order
- `npm run factory:tick` still works locally on Windows

### Why
Qodo on PR 100: the `/factory` gate for `revert:check` is only in the agent's instructions, so an agent that reports ready after exit 1 or 2 isn't stopped by the runner. Day 4's lesson was that the runner checks effects instead of taking the agent's word; this applies it to the new check.

### Out of scope
- A real sandbox for agent-written tests (no network, a separate user, resource limits): the charter's Devil's Advocate work

### Depends on
#64, #67

issues.title: Prove our tests catch the bugs they were written for
issues.body:
### Result
A check that proves our tests catch the bugs they were written for. For every fix that came from a review finding, it undoes the fix in a scratch copy and runs the tests. A test must fail each time. If one doesn't, that test proves nothing.

### Done when
- [ ] `npm run mutation:check` reads a list of fixes (commit, files changed, the test that should catch it) kept in the repo
- [ ] For each fix it undoes only the code change, not the test, in a scratch copy, runs the tests, and reports "caught" or "not caught" by name
- [ ] It exits non-zero if any fix is not caught, and never changes the working tree
- [ ] The list covers every fix from Day 3 that was reproduced with a failing test, in both repos
- [ ] Run once: the result (caught out of total) is in the PR, and every "not caught" either gets a better test or an explained entry
- [ ] It runs in CI in both repos

### Must not break
- `npm run check` stays fast: the mutation check is its own CI job
- The target's copy says nothing about this repo or about planted bugs: it reads like an ordinary test-quality check
- The working tree and git history are never changed (scratch copy only, no force push)

### Why
FaultForge plants bugs to test a reviewer. We should do the same to our own tests. On Day 3 every finding was reproduced with a failing test before it was fixed, but only once, by hand, at that moment. On target 15 we showed by hand that the tests fail when the code is wrong. Nothing checks that this stays true as the code changes.

### Out of scope
- Random mutations of every line (a mutation testing framework). This only undoes real fixes.

### Depends on
None

issues.title: Block merging until Qodo's review is complete
issues.body:
### Result
A required "Qodo review" check that stays pending until Qodo's API says the review of the PR's current commit is complete. No PR can be merged on a review that is still being written.

### Done when
- [ ] A workflow polls Qodo's read-only API (`get-pr-review-findings`) and passes only when the review session's commit is the PR's head commit and its status is `completed`
- [ ] Its summary lists the open findings for that commit, with severity and title
- [ ] It fails, with a clear message, if the review isn't complete after 20 minutes
- [ ] It is required in `protect-main` here, and the same check runs in the target through its own ticket
- [ ] Shown on a real PR: the check is pending while Qodo is still working, and passes once the API says complete

### Must not break
- Only read-only Qodo calls; the API key is an Actions secret and is never printed
- Qodo's own configuration is unchanged: this only reads from it
- The target's copy doesn't refer to this repo (no shared workflow, no link)
- CI (`npm run check`) still runs and is still required

### Why
On Day 3, Qodo posted "no open findings" twice and then edited the same comment minutes later to add a High finding (PR 55). A PR must not look finished before the reviewer is.

### Depends on
#5

issues.title: Epic: one factory loop for both repos
issues.body:
### Result
Both repos are built the same way, top-down: charter → milestone → epic → tickets in either repo → one branch and PR each → CI → Qodo → live check → evidence. The owner approves tickets, merges PRs and confirms verdicts; everything in between runs as a loop.

### Tickets, in order
- [x] #46
- [x] #47
- [x] #17
- [x] #48
- [x] #5
- [ ] #56
- [ ] #49
- [x] #50
- [x] target 10: run the checks on every pull request (plain text, not a link)
- [ ] target 11: say what must not break in every ticket (changes AGENTS.md, so a new Qodo configuration version)
- [ ] target 13: wait for the code review before merging (plain text, not a link)

### Must not break
- The target never links to this repo: no parent issues, no board, no mentions
- The owner stays the final authority: no automatic merges or verdicts

### Why
Day 3 showed two factories in one project: the tool and the product. They should work the same way, and the tool should run its own work through the loop it measures.

- [ ] Tested against saved API responses, no network

The top-down view lives here, so the target never has to link back.

### Result
`faultforge replay` re-runs everything from saved Qodo output.

### Done when
- [ ] Only the Qodo call is replaced
- [ ] Output marked as replayed
- [ ] Same numbers as the report
- [ ] No Qodo account needed

### Why
Judges can reproduce the results.

### Depends on
#20, #31

issues.title: Qodo reviews the generated tests
issues.body:
### Result
A generated test counts only after Qodo has reviewed it.

### Done when
- [ ] Tests go through a Qodo review
- [ ] Review saved with the challenge

### Why
Qodo stays the reviewer.

### Depends on
#28, #16

issues.title: Owner approves hidden findings
issues.body:
### Result
The owner signs off every hidden or unclear finding.

### Done when
- [ ] Lists what's waiting, with evidence
- [ ] Approve or reject with a reason
- [ ] Hidden findings can always be viewed

### Why
The human has the final say.

### Depends on
#31

issues.title: Arbiter v1
issues.body:
### Result
A plain function decides what reaches the developer.

### Done when
- [ ] Checks the evidence exists and matches the snapshot
- [ ] Security findings never hidden without the owner
- [ ] Every decision logged with a reason
- [ ] Tests for every route

### Why
No finding dropped because a model disagreed.

### Depends on
#30

issues.title: Check the test hits the claimed problem
issues.body:
### Result
A passing test only counts if it reaches the code in question.

### Done when
- [ ] Checks the test reaches the affected code
- [ ] Compares fixed and broken versions where possible
- [ ] Otherwise the verdict is inconclusive

### Why
A passing test is not proof.

### Depends on
#28

issues.title: First challenge on a real finding
issues.body:
### Result
Devil's Advocate challenges a finding from a real case.

### Done when
- [ ] Result saved with the case
- [ ] Owner reviews it
- [ ] Written up in the decision log

### Why
Day 15 milestone.

### Depends on
#28, #11

issues.title: Devil's Advocate v1
issues.body:
### Result
Takes one Qodo finding, writes a test for it, runs it and proposes a verdict.

### Done when
- [ ] Never sees the answer key
- [ ] Saves the hypothesis, test, commands and output
- [ ] Verdict: supported, disproven or inconclusive
- [ ] Supports FF-0001's finding with a failing test

### Why
Proof, not opinion.

### Depends on
#27

issues.title: Sandbox for generated tests
issues.body:
### Result
Generated tests run in a throwaway place.

### Done when
- [ ] Time and memory limits
- [ ] No network, no credentials
- [ ] Records commands, exit code and output

### Why
We run generated code.

### Depends on
#15

issues.title: First audit of another project
issues.body:
### Result
A blind-spot report on a TypeScript project I own.

### Done when
- [ ] Local clone or own fork only, no PRs elsewhere
- [ ] Each defect placed in the tests vs review grid
- [ ] Defects that change nothing are left out

### Why
The tool should work on real code.

### Depends on
#23

issues.title: Export public case records
issues.body:
### Result
Every judged case can be published.

### Done when
- [ ] `faultforge export` writes `examples/<case>.json`
- [ ] Judged cases only
- [ ] Test that nothing private leaks

### Why
Every result must be checkable.

### Depends on
#3, #11

issues.title: Write down the evaluation method
issues.body:
### Result
`docs/evaluation-method.md` defines every number we report.

### Done when
- [ ] Each metric with its denominator
- [ ] Matches what the report computes
- [ ] Linked from the README

### Why
Definitions before results.

### Depends on
#20

issues.title: Generic templates for any TypeScript project
issues.body:
### Result
Templates that work on code we've never seen.

### Done when
- [ ] At least 6: remove a guard, flip a comparison, drop an await, remove an auth check, swallow an error, shift a boundary
- [ ] Each one compiles after the change

### Why
Needed for the audit command.

### Depends on
#9

issues.title: Tag repeats and held-out cases
issues.body:
### Result
Repeated templates can't inflate the numbers.

### Done when
- [ ] Each case tagged new, repeat or held-out
- [ ] Report shows them apart
- [ ] Order comes from a recorded seed

### Why
Repeats look better than they are.

### Depends on
#20

issues.title: Freeze benchmark v1
issues.body:
### Result
A fixed baseline to compare against.

### Done when
- [ ] Config, templates, match rule and review source recorded
- [ ] Any change starts v2

### Why
No changes mid-measurement.

### Depends on
#6, #18

issues.title: Report command
issues.body:
### Result
`faultforge report` shows the results from the audit log.

### Done when
- [ ] Catch rate and precision as counts with denominators
- [ ] Split by config, review source and bug type
- [ ] Counts only when the sample is small

### Why
Only measured numbers.

### Depends on
#19

issues.title: Get Qodo to review FaultForge's own PRs
issues.body:
### Result
Qodo reviews this repo without seeing it during target reviews.

### Done when
- [ ] Options tried
- [ ] One chosen, with proof it doesn't reach target reviews
- [ ] Decision log and `CLAUDE.md` updated

### Why
We cut Qodo's access on Day 1.

### Depends on
#6

### Notes
- Day 1 removed Qodo's access to this repo because it linked the two repos and could read lab content during target reviews (see decision log).
- Options: Qodo local review of diffs here; or access again plus the #4 check before every case.
- Prove it: after the change, run the #4 check and confirm no links and no rules from this repo.

issues.title: Move the engine into a core package
issues.body:
### Result
`packages/core` holds the engine. CLI and scripts call into it.

### Done when
- [ ] Target and review source are interfaces
- [ ] Inject, capture and match use them
- [ ] Existing tests still pass

### Why
Same engine for CLI, replay, Action and a later app.

### Depends on
#5

### Notes
- Charter §15.3. Move logic from `packages/harness/src/` into `packages/core/src/`; harness keeps the CLI entry points.
- Two interfaces: `Target` (clone, apply, test) and `ReviewSource` (get findings for a change). One implementation each for now.

issues.title: Run more bug cases
issues.body:
### Result
More cases across different kinds of bugs.

### Done when
- [ ] At least 4 more cases judged
- [ ] At least 3 kinds of bugs
- [ ] Same config for all

### Why
One case is a story, not a benchmark.

### Depends on
#4, #5, #8, #12

### Notes
- Use `/new-case`. Write each template in `private/templates/` first.
- Spread across invariants in the target's `INVARIANTS.md`. Don't repeat the FF-0001 template here.

issues.title: Run the first control cases
issues.body:
### Result
Harmless changes go through the same pipeline.

### Done when
- [ ] At least 2 control cases run
- [ ] Every finding on them judged by the owner

### Why
No precision without controls.

### Depends on
#12

### Notes
- A control is a real, harmless change with its own ticket: a refactor, a small feature, a doc fix.
- Every finding on a control needs the owner's judgement: real problem, false alarm or open. None are assumed false.

issues.title: Link a target ticket to every case PR
issues.body:
### Result
Case PRs link a ticket, like real PRs do.

### Done when
- [ ] Decision log records the new config version first
- [ ] `/new-case` creates the ticket and adds `Closes #N`
- [ ] Ticket text saved with the case
- [ ] Control PRs get tickets too

### Why
Real PRs have tickets. Mixing would break comparisons.

### Depends on
#9, #4

### Notes
- Files: `.claude/skills/new-case/SKILL.md`, `inject.ts`
- Write the decision log entry (new config version and how requirement-gap findings are matched) before the first ticketed case.
- Target ticket text must pass the guard hook; it describes the change, never the bug.

issues.title: One branch per case
issues.body:
### Result
A template can run again on a newer target commit.

### Done when
- [ ] Branch name made per case
- [ ] Names still look ordinary
- [ ] Old case branches are kept

### Why
Needed for repeat runs.

### Notes
- Files: `packages/harness/src/inject.ts`, `templates/seed/*/template.json` (`publish.branch`)
- Build the name from the template's neutral wording plus a short suffix, e.g. `tidy-replay-lookup-2`. Check it with `neutral.ts`.

issues.title: End-to-end tests for inject
issues.body:
### Result
Tests catch a broken inject command.

### Done when
- [ ] Full inject on a temp clone of the target
- [ ] A bad template is refused and the clone is left clean
- [ ] Runs in `npm run check`

### Why
On Day 1 inject broke and the checks still passed.

### Notes
- Files: `packages/harness/src/inject.ts`, new `packages/harness/src/inject.e2e.test.ts`
- Use `FAULTFORGE_PRIVATE_DIR` pointed at a temp folder, and a small fixture template whose proof test does or doesn't fail.
- The failure path (branch undo) has never run; expect a bug there.

issues.title: Pick the review source and measure variance
issues.body:
### Result
We know how reviews are collected and how much they change between runs.

### Done when
- [ ] Local Qodo review tried: works, gated or unavailable
- [ ] Same diff reviewed 3 times, differences recorded
- [ ] Decision in the decision log

### Why
Charter Day 2 gate.

### Depends on
#5

### Notes
- Charter §10 has the 7-step check. Qodo's review skill doc is linked in the charter references.
- Variance: same diff, three runs. Use a new branch per run so each is a fresh PR review, and record the time and every finding.
- Each review run counts against quota; note the usage.

issues.title: Check Qodo's setup before each case
issues.body:
### Result
One command confirms Qodo matches the saved config.

### Done when
- [ ] Compares rules and skills with the saved snapshot
- [ ] Fails if any repo is linked to the target
- [ ] Read-only API calls only
- [ ] `/new-case` runs it first
- [ ] Tests for match, changed rule, extra rule

### Why
On Day 2 a push to the target changed Qodo's rules.

### Notes
- Files: new `packages/harness/src/qodo-check.ts`, script `qodo:check` in `package.json`
- Read-only client: `private/qodo-mcp-readonly.mjs` (tools `rules-list`, `review-skills-list`, `cross-repo-overview`). Snapshot: `private/config/qodo-v3/`.
- Compare by rule id, content and state. Ignore timestamps and counters like `updatedAt`.
- The key file path comes from `QODO_KEY_FILE`; never print the key.

issues.title: Block unreviewed case names in public issues and PRs
issues.body:
### Result
The guard hook stops issues or PRs here from naming a case or template that hasn't been reviewed yet.

### Done when
- [ ] Reads names from private storage at run time, nothing secret in this repo
- [ ] Allows everything when `private/` is missing
- [ ] Tests for blocked, allowed and missing folder

### Why
The plan is public. Which bug comes next is not.

### Notes
- Files: `.claude/hooks/guard-target.ts`, `packages/harness/src/neutral.ts`
- Add a second check for `gh issue|pr ... --repo AJBeumer/faultforge`. Names come from `private/templates/*` folder names and case ids in `private/ground-truth.jsonl` that have no `case.adjudicated` event in `private/audit-events.jsonl`.
- Keep the hook fast: read the files only when the command targets this repo.
